nodes.label: SPIKE-0 — no library exposes an XSD component model
nodes.rationale: Resolved by survey rather than experiment. A positive answer would have removed roughly 40% of the engineering budget. The consequence is the whole product thesis: 'what may I put here?' is not a validation feature, because no validator exposes the state machine that answers it.

nodes.label: SPIKE-1 — libxml2-wasm reports all errors, with line numbers; columns are always 0
nodes.rationale: Measured against libxml2-wasm@0.7.1 with five faults in five sibling subtrees. Confirms the lineMap design and removes the need for xmllint-wasm. A structural failure truncates the rest of that element, so the Problems panel must not promise to be exhaustive after the first structural error in a subtree.

nodes.label: SPIKE-2 — multi-file schema sets work through a registered input provider
nodes.rationale: xmlRegisterInputProvider resolves both import and include, so no flattening is needed and the fallback the plan had budgeted for is unnecessary. The provider is also the security boundary: match and open only answer for keys already in the catalogue, so there is no code path from a hostile schemaLocation to the network.

nodes.label: SPIKE-3 — Glushkov automaton latency, partially answered
nodes.rationale: Sub-millisecond on every schema in the test suite, but the UBL 2.1 / GML 3.2 criterion waits on the corpus. The position budget marks a model approximate rather than pretending to be exact. insertionPlan deliberately does not share the single-sweep optimisation and is quadratic in child count, which is fine for one element's palette and is why it is not used to paint the tree.

nodes.label: SPIKE-4 — mixed content: neither candidate, and the spike asked the wrong question
nodes.rationale: Both candidate answers were editors, but the unusable part was never the editing — it was the display. Five rows is unreadable before anyone types anything, so the change that mattered is that a mixed element is one tree row carrying its flow.

nodes.label: Scoped source snippet flow editor
nodes.rationale: Inner XML in a textarea with the schema's permitted inline elements as wrap buttons, and nothing committed until it parses. Refusing a broken commit matters more here than anywhere else, because the alternative is discarding a paragraph someone was midway through typing.

nodes.label: ProseMirror declined
nodes.rationale: ~150 KB in the entry chunk plus a second document model to keep in step with the CST — the exact two-representations problem this codebase is arranged around, bought for a minority of documents. Risk 4 has already fired once in this project for less. What is given up is WYSIWYG.

nodes.label: libxml2-wasm needs an ES-module worker (worker: { format: 'es' })
nodes.rationale: libxml2-wasm initialises with a top-level await, which Vite's default iife worker output cannot express. The failure is a build error rather than a runtime one so it cannot reach production, but it costs an afternoon if met without warning.

nodes.label: Differential harness finding: abstract substitution-group head accepted
nodes.rationale: The palette already excluded abstract candidates from insertion but the validation path did not, so the engine would have called a document valid that libxml2 rejects. The fix pushes abstract down onto the element particle — filtering at the palette was treating a symptom — and the naive reference matcher used by the property tests now encodes the same rule so the two oracles stay in step.

nodes.label: Security model asserted rather than assumed
nodes.rationale: packages/xsd-libxml2/test/engine.test.ts feeds a billion-laughs bomb and an XXE payload pointing at file:///etc/passwd and checks that the first returns promptly instead of expanding and the second never yields the file's contents.
